review_notes: Read the whole target file and checked Mathlib's MvPolynomial API (`as_sum`, `linearMap_ext`, `coeffsIn`, `mem_coeffsIn`). Found no existing Mathlib lemma that expresses `F p = ∑ α ∈ p.support, p.coeff α • F (monomial α 1)` for a linear map F. `linearMap_ext` needs agreement on all monomials, but the two `_of_reduced` theorems only have a hypothesis on `p.support`, so it doesn't replace the helper. I also looked at the uses in docs and tests. `monomial_eq_smul_one`, `linearDivision_remainder_of_reduced` and `linearDivision_quotient_of_reduced` are mentioned in docs/API.md and the tests, so a new helper would have to be added next to them. The rewrites in the finding are sketches I haven't compiled. The main uncertainty is how much each of the four proofs shrinks. The `of_reduced` pair gains the most.

findings.problem: Four proofs repeat the same reduction of a linear map to monomials. They expand `p` with `p.as_sum`, distribute with `map_sum`, rewrite each term as `coeff • monomial α 1` with `monomial_eq_smul_one`, and push the map through with `map_smul`. The two `_of_reduced` theorems (lines 200–229) are almost line-for-line copies: each is a sum over `p.support` followed by `rw [monomial_eq_smul_one, map_smul]` and a monomial lemma. The same reduction appears in `linearMap_preserves_coeffsIn` (lines 172–177) and, with an explicit calc, in `linearDivision_decomposition` (lines 103–124). Each proof redoes the `conv_lhs => rw [p.as_sum]` / `rw [map_sum]` bookkeeping and the `Finset.sum_congr` scaffolding. `MvPolynomial.linearMap_ext` doesn't cover this case: the `_of_reduced` theorems only know the behaviour on `p.support`, not on all monomials.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general lemma, placed after `monomial_eq_smul_one`:

lemma linearMap_apply_eq_sum {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    (F : MvPolynomial σ R →ₗ[R] M) (p : MvPolynomial σ R) :
    F p = ∑ α ∈ p.support, p.coeff α • F (monomial α (1 : R)) := by
  classical
  conv_lhs => rw [p.as_sum]
  rw [map_sum]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun α _ => by
    rw [monomial_eq_smul_one α (p.coeff α), map_smul]

Proof sketch: expand `p` as the sum of its monomials, apply additivity, then pull the scalar out of each `monomial α (coeff α)`. Then rewrite the uses:
- `linearDivision_remainder_of_reduced`: `rw [linearMap_apply_eq_sum (linearDivisionRemainder m b hb) p]; conv_rhs => rw [p.as_sum]; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun α hα => by rw [linearDivisionRemainder_monomial, ((basisDivision m b hb α).2.2.2 (hp α hα)).2, ← monomial_eq_smul_one]`.
- `linearDivision_quotient_of_reduced`: `rw [linearMap_apply_eq_sum (linearDivisionQuotient m b hb) p]; exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun α hα => by rw [linearDivisionQuotient_monomial, ((basisDivision m b hb α).2.2.2 (hp α hα)).1, smul_zero]`.
- `linearMap_preserves_coeffsIn`: `rw [linearMap_apply_eq_sum F p]; refine Submodule.sum_mem _ fun α _ => ?_`, then `rw [mem_coeffsIn]; intro β; rw [coeff_smul, smul_eq_mul]; exact J.mul_mem_right _ (hp α)`. This drops the `as_sum`/`map_sum`/`map_smul` steps and keeps only the ideal argument.
- `linearDivision_decomposition`: apply the lemma to `(Finsupp.linearCombination (MvPolynomial σ R) b).restrictScalars R ∘ₗ linearDivisionQuotient m b hb` and to `linearDivisionRemainder m b hb`. Then use `basisDivision .. |>.2.1` termwise instead of the manual `hsmul` and `map_sum` calc.
findings.benefit: The monomial-expansion argument is proved once instead of four times. The `of_reduced` proofs reduce to the actual mathematical content, namely that the chosen witnesses on reduced monomials are trivial. Maintenance is also easier: any change to how `linearDivisionQuotient` or `linearDivisionRemainder` is defined or simplified affects one helper instead of four hand-written sum manipulations.
